abstract: Intermediate filaments elongate by end-to-end annealing of filament subunits. We develop a Smoluchowski coagulation model with a single kinetic parameter, k0, that reproduces data from time-resolved atomic force microscopy, electron microscopy, and static light scattering. The model predicts log-normal filament length distributions, sublinear filament growth, and saturation of scattering intensity ratios. For a given protein, the inferred assembly rate constants agree across measurement techniques
